newsitem.title: USA: Florida jobless rate hits nine-year low in January.
newsitem.headline: Florida jobless rate hits nine-year low in January.

text.p: Florida's unemployemnt rate dropped to 4.8 percent in January, down from 4.9 percent in December and 5.4 percent a year ago, the state Department of Labor and Employment Security said Tuesday.

The jobless rate was Florida's lowest since May 1988 and represents 340,000 unemployed Floridians out of a civilian labor force of 7.09 million. Total nonfarm employment for January was 6.29 million, an increase of 235,300 jobs or 3.9 percent from January of last year.
Services gained the most jobs, 112,500, and had the highest growth rate, 5.5 percent, over the year.
Trade added 57,300 jobs, construction added 8,500, and manufacturing gained 6,000 jobs over the year.

The transportation, communications and public utilities sector increased by 12,500 jobs, with transportation accounting for most of the gains. Those gains more than offset the loss of 1,300 utilities jobs as electric and gas utilities laid off workers in anticipation of tougher competition under deregulation, the department said.
Finance, insurance and real estate gained 15,900 jobs over the year, while government gained 22,400.
All of Florida's metropolitan areas had job increases over last year. Orlando added the most jobs, 47,200, and had the fastest job growth, 6.5 percent. Miami had the slowest growth rate, 2.6 percent.

Monroe County had the lowest unemployment rate, 2.4 percent, while Taylor County ahd the highest, 12.9 percent. Of Florida's 67 counties, 52 had a decline in their unemployement rate from last January.
